recommendation: Keep the commit as-is because it is a narrow consistency fix for an already-applied Jira decision. Further work is only needed if Patient Care later reopens the semantic question and chooses a breaking datatype or value-set change.
issue_request: FHIR-55315 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. Patient Care voted to add an unknown code to the AdverseEvent.actuality code system and value set, define it as indicating that the source system does not specify which current value applies, and add a comment that use is unusual, legacy-data-oriented, and strongly discouraged.
initial_application: HL7/fhir commits 78171f260c82d2a9f4db6b4074ca3bd791f368b2 and eb5350e6f879455be0ebe678bedf3d2014f8186c applied most of the change by adding the unknown concept, updating the AdverseEvent.actuality short display and comment, and recording J#55315 in committee notes. The value set composes the complete code system, so the terminology was otherwise in place.
additional_context: BRR input initially favored a boolean/two-value model, but the later Patient Care Jira resolution chose the compatible unknown-code escape valve for legacy data. source/fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent active in the current build, and the search parameter bundle under source/adverseevent is a current build input. Searches found no Zulip or high-signal Confluence evidence reversing the Jira decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/adverseevent/bundle-AdverseEvent-search-params.xml so the AdverseEvent-actuality SearchParameter description now lists actual, potential, and unknown.
source_changes: source/adverseevent/bundle-AdverseEvent-search-params.xml: updated the AdverseEvent-actuality SearchParameter description from "actual | potential" to "actual | potential | unknown".
